description.fun: Turtwig's shell isn't bone but soil, which hardens when it drinks water and feels slightly damp on a healthy one. It makes its own food by photosynthesis across its whole body, and the little leaf on its head wilts when it's thirsty. It is also the heaviest of every first-stage starter, a solid 10.2 kg of turtle.
description.guide: Turtwig is a small Grass-type turtle and one of the three first partner Pokémon of Sinnoh. Its shell is made of soil that hardens when it drinks, and it photosynthesizes through its whole body. It evolves into Grotle and then Torterra.
description.tagline: Sinnoh's Grass starter: a little turtle with a shell of soil.

description.fun: Grotle carries a small grove on its back: two bushes grow from its shell of hardened soil, and their sweet berries draw other Pokémon to peck at them. Every Grotle is said to have its own secret spring of clean water, and it carries fellow Pokémon there on its back. By day it leaves the forest so its shrubs can soak up the sun.
description.guide: Grotle is the evolved form of Turtwig, a Grass-type turtle whose soil shell carries two berry-bearing bushes. It lives near clean water in forests and is said to know secret springs, carrying other Pokémon to them on its back. It evolves into Torterra.
description.tagline: A walking garden that knows where the clean springs are.

description.fun: Torterra is a living landscape: a tree and three rocky peaks rise from its shell, and small Pokémon nest there, some spending their whole lives on its back. Herds migrating in search of water have been mistaken for moving forests. Ancient people imagined a gigantic Torterra living beneath the ground, much like the World Turtle of old myths that carries the world on its back.
description.guide: Torterra is the final form of Turtwig, a Grass- and Ground-type tortoise with an oak-like tree and stony peaks growing from its shell. Small Pokémon often nest on its back, and migrating herds have been mistaken for moving forests.
description.tagline: A tortoise with a whole forest, and its residents, on its back.
